baselineFindings.title: Inherited SUBSWITCH_CONFIG can redirect the existing init smoke outside the fixture
baselineFindings.evidence: The new metadata command and both serve commands override SUBSWITCH_CONFIG only for their child processes. The later init command sets CODEX_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME but leaves any inherited SUBSWITCH_CONFIG intact. src/codex-init.ts:30-35 prefers that value over XDG_CONFIG_HOME; lines 85-89 read the selected config and lines 252-258 write the setup plan there. Thus a developer running the smoke with SUBSWITCH_CONFIG already set can read/change that external config despite the temporary install directory. The affected init invocation is unchanged from the assigned base.
baselineFindings.impact: Pre-existing developer-environment isolation gap; does not invalidate the recorded clean-environment red/green smoke or clean GitHub runners. No foreign configuration was read or modified during this review.
baselineFindings.recommendedFollowup: Have the owning package/smoke worker explicitly select a fixture-owned SUBSWITCH_CONFIG for init and verify an inherited sentinel path remains untouched. Track this separately or include it in a follow-up delta; do not claim the entire existing script is hermetic under arbitrary inherited environment.
